annotations.keyFindings: Highest against lowest continuity quintile: unplanned admissions rate ratio 0.84 in adults aged 65 and over, 0.76 for ambulatory care-sensitive conditions, after adjustment for age, sex, chronic conditions and prior admissions.
annotations.limitations: Observational; residual confounding by severity; one health system.

annotations.keyFindings: Personal lists raised continuity from 0.46 to 0.61; emergency admissions fell 6 percent against trend with an interval including no change; routine waits rose from 6 to 9 days.
annotations.limitations: No comparison practices; co-intervention in the same period.
annotations.notes: The only study that changed continuity on purpose.

claims.text: Among adults aged 65 and over, the highest continuity quintile had fewer unplanned admissions than the lowest after adjustment for chronic conditions and prior admissions.
claims.passage: Patients in the highest continuity quintile had fewer unplanned admissions in the second year than those in the lowest (rate ratio 0.84, 95 percent CI 0.79 to 0.90)
claims.interpretation: An association worth reviewing systematically; confounding by severity remains.

claims.text: When practices raised continuity deliberately with personal lists, emergency admissions changed by an amount compatible with no change, and routine waits lengthened.
claims.passage: Emergency admissions among them fell by 6 percent relative to the pre-existing trend (95 percent CI -1 to 12 percent), an estimate compatible with no change.
claims.interpretation: Intervention evidence is thin and waits are a real cost.

synthesis: Two retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. A large population study found fewer unplanned admissions with higher continuity among older adults after adjustment, strongest for ambulatory care-sensitive conditions, but residual confounding by severity is likely. The only study that raised continuity deliberately found an admissions change compatible with no effect and longer waits. Two records cannot answer the question; they justify a full systematic search.
gradeRationale: Two observational studies, one uncontrolled with an imprecise estimate; serious risk of confounding and imprecision.
summary: Two retrieved records appraised; two claims recorded; overall certainty very low.
